title: Shortest Path in UG with unit weights
problemStatement: Given an undirected graph with n nodes (0…n-1) where every edge has weight 1, and a source src, return the shortest-path distance from src to every node. Unreachable nodes should be −1.
intuition: When every edge costs 1, BFS explores level by level. The first time you reach a node is via a minimum number of edges — so queue order = distance order. No priority queue needed (unlike Dijkstra).

approaches.title: Brute: DFS with path length / re-explore
approaches.idea: Try all simple paths and keep the minimum length. Correct but exponential / messy on general graphs.
limitations: Do not use in interviews as the solution

approaches.title: Optimal: BFS distances
approaches.idea: dist[src]=0; BFS. When you first discover v from u, set dist[v]=dist[u]+1. Never revisit.
algorithm: While queue: pop u; for each unseen neighbor v: dist[v]=dist[u]+1; enqueue v
approaches.whyWorks: Unit weights ⇒ every edge advances distance by exactly 1. BFS never finds a shorter path later.

python.notes: Undirected: add both directions. dist[v] < 0 means unseen.

specialTechnique.title: When BFS is enough
specialTechnique.body:
Unweighted / unit weights → BFS
0-1 weights → 0-1 BFS (deque)
Non-negative weights → Dijkstra
Negative weights → Bellman-Ford
DAG → topo + relax

edgeCases: Self-loop / duplicate edges (harmless if you mark visited via dist)
commonMistakes: Forgetting to add both undirected directions
Updating dist again after first visit (BFS already optimal)
followUps: Reconstruct one shortest path via parent[]?
0-1 BFS when weights are only 0 or 1?
interviewInsight: Say out loud: “Unit weights ⇒ BFS; first touch is shortest.”
